title: Art of War
description: Lead your ancient army in a chess-style tactical battle inspired by Sun Tzu's Art of War. Command your General, War Elephant, Cavalry, Archers, Catapults, and Infantry across an 8x8 battlefield. Capture enemy forces, seize forts and river crossings, and build your war treasury to 10 million to claim total victory on the ancient battlefield.
learning_objectives: Develop strategic thinking by applying ancient military principles to tactical board control
Practice resource management by balancing troop movements with territorial acquisition
Learn the importance of terrain advantage through controlling high ground and river crossings
Build risk assessment skills by evaluating when to advance, hold position, or retreat
Understand Sun Tzu's principles of deception, patience, and knowing your enemy
Strengthen long-term planning by coordinating diverse military units toward multiple victory conditions
how_to_play: Each turn you receive 2 Action Points (AP). Moving a unit costs 1 AP, and using a special ability costs AP as listed on the ability.
Units move like chess pieces: General=King, War Elephant=Queen, Cavalry=Rook, Archer=Bishop, Catapult=Knight, Infantry=Pawn.
Engage enemy units by moving onto their square to deal damage. Infantry promote to War Elephant when reaching the far side of the battlefield.
Control resource tiles by positioning your troops on them. Each tile generates war funds every turn.
Win by capturing the enemy General, controlling 3 or more resource tiles, or accumulating 10 million in your war treasury.
Use special abilities wisely: each unit has two unique abilities rooted in ancient military doctrine that can shift the tide of battle.
objectives: Capture the rival General to achieve an instant decisive victory
Control 3 or more strategic resource tiles for a territorial dominance victory
Build your war treasury to 10 million through strategic income and conquest

storybook_pages.title: The Ancient Battlefield
storybook_pages.text: Two rival warlords meet on the field of destiny. The terrain is dotted with forts, river crossings, and high ground — each providing a critical advantage to whoever controls them. Sun Tzu wrote that every battle is won before it is ever fought. Study the terrain, know your enemy, and deploy your forces with wisdom.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: two ancient Chinese armies facing each other across an 8x8 battlefield grid with forts, rivers, and mountains, ink wash painting style with golden dramatic lighting, epic scale

storybook_pages.title: Your Army
storybook_pages.text:
General (King) - Your supreme commander, if he falls the army crumbles.
War Elephant (Queen) - Unstoppable force that moves in any direction.
Cavalry (Rook) - Swift horsemen that charge in straight lines.
Archer (Bishop) - Deadly diagonal rain of arrows from across the field.
Catapult (Knight) - Siege weapon with unpredictable L-shaped bombardment.
Infantry (Pawn) - The backbone of your army, capable of promotion to War Elephant!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: lineup of six ancient military units: a general in ornate armor, a war elephant with a howdah, cavalry on horseback, an archer drawing a bow, a siege catapult, and infantry with shields, detailed historical illustration style

storybook_pages.title: The Terrain Advantage
storybook_pages.text: The battlefield holds 6 strategic positions: the Fort provides defensive strength, the River Crossing controls movement, the Supply Depot feeds your army, the High Ground offers unmatched visibility, the Bridge connects key flanks, and the Granary sustains prolonged campaigns. As Sun Tzu taught: occupy the advantageous ground first.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: birds eye view of an ancient battlefield grid with six glowing strategic locations showing a stone fort, river crossing, supply wagons, hilltop position, stone bridge, and granary, painted map style with classical Chinese art influences

rounds.title: Art of War
rounds.story: The ancient battlefield awaits your command. Deploy your forces with the wisdom of Sun Tzu, seize strategic terrain, and crush your rival before they outmaneuver you!
rounds.coaching_moment: Think carefully about the trade-offs before committing to this path.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What sacrifices did you make, and were they worth it?

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

cultural_context: Chess is believed to have originated in India as Chaturanga over 1,500 years ago, making strategic board games deeply embedded in Indian intellectual culture. Sun Tzu's principles of indirect action and resource conservation are studied in India's leading management institutes and military academies.
reflection_prompt: What pattern did your opponent rely on, and how did you counter (or fail to)?
